data.mechanism: A competing model: the enzyme that loads leucine onto tRNA doubles as the leucine sensor, binding free leucine directly.
data.mechanism_beginner: One competing idea: the enzyme that loads leucine onto its transport molecule for protein-building doubles as the leucine sensor.
data.boundary: Proposed before the Sestrin2 model and never cleanly reconciled with it.

conflict.basis: A competing model, not an opposing result, and the distinction is the reason the conflicting-studies list here is empty. HAN2012 proposes leucyl-tRNA synthetase as the intracellular leucine sensor for mTORC1. WOL2015 and SAX2015 identify Sestrin2 as a leucine sensor and are carried on their own edge (LEU-SESN2). Neither of those studies tested LARS and found it not to bind leucine, so neither is a conflicting result on this claim; they establish a second candidate sensor that the field has never reconciled with the first head-to-head. No study in this corpus has tested the two models against each other, which is why this edge is marked contested while listing no conflicting study.

data.note: CONTESTED with LEU-SESN2. Two published leucine sensors, both from strong labs, never resolved head-to-head. Prime Contradiction Engine seed.
